narrativeReportMd:
# BodyStructure R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
BodyStructure has material local breaking changes. R6 keeps the same resource identity but remodels R4's flat anatomy fields into a required repeating `includedStructure` backbone and adds R6-only anatomy detail. Direct R4 instances using root `location`, `morphology`, or `locationQualifier`, or omitting any location, require transformation before R6 validation.

## Scope
The report uses the local R4/R6 core StructureDefinitions, package metadata/indexes, assignment manifest, directly referenced ValueSets, and primitive definitions for the `description` type change. Inherited base-resource and base-datatype changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Treat migration as a resource reshape, not a simple rename. Build `includedStructure` entries, move morphology under the relevant structure, classify qualifiers into qualifier versus laterality versus landmark-orientation data, and define explicit R6-to-R4 policy for patientless and richly localized R6 instances.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are the required `includedStructure.structure` model, the move of `morphology`, and the split of `locationQualifier`. These are hard structural breaks for serialized instances and generated-code paths.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for records without an R4 location, qualifier-to-laterality mapping, multiple anatomy structures, and terminology changes where no ConceptMap or SNOMED expansion was available.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most breaking changes appear tied to a justified richer anatomy model. They could have been phased in with deprecated root aliases, cross-version extensions, or ConceptMaps, but that would leave duplicate representations and reconciliation rules.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 BodyStructure has the same canonical identity but a substantially different local content model. Top concerns are the mandatory `includedStructure.structure`, moved/split root anatomy fields, and lossy R6-to-R4 conversion for patientless or richly localized R6 instances. Main uncertainty is terminology mapping because no official ConceptMap or live SNOMED expansion was available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Build `includedStructure` from R4 `location`, move `morphology` into that structure, classify `locationQualifier` values into laterality/qualifier/landmark-orientation destinations, and update generated-code paths, FHIRPath expressions, persistence schemas, UI pick lists, and down-conversion rules.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, type, flag, and local-constraint findings because they are directly visible in the StructureDefinitions. Confidence is medium for terminology impact because packaged ValueSet compose definitions were compared without live SNOMED expansions or official ConceptMaps.

findings.title: Anatomical location moved from optional root element to required includedStructure.structure

oldState.summary: R4 had optional top-level `BodyStructure.location` 0..1 CodeableConcept and no required local anatomical-site element.

binding.description: Codes describing anatomical locations. May include laterality.

semanticText.definition: The anatomical location or region of the specimen, lesion, or body structure.

oldState.narrativeMd: A minimal R4 BodyStructure could be valid with the required `patient` and no coded location.

newState.summary: R6 requires `BodyStructure.includedStructure` 1..*, and each includedStructure requires `structure` 1..1 CodeableConcept.

semanticText.short: Code that represents the included structure
semanticText.definition: Code that represents the included structure.

newState.narrativeMd: The anatomical location is now nested in a required repeating backbone.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The definitions and body-site binding align, but R6 nests the site under a mandatory repeating backbone.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 instances that omit `location`, or that still carry root-level `location`, do not satisfy the R6 requirement for at least one `includedStructure.structure`. Generated R4 clients expose `location` at the resource root, while R6 clients expose a repeating backbone.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Wrong or missing anatomical location can change clinical interpretation of observations, specimens, lesions, or imaging-related data.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow one BodyStructure to describe multiple included anatomic structures with per-structure detail.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated root `location` while adding `includedStructure` with consistency or precedence rules.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal, supporting multiple included anatomic structures with per-structure detail and an explicit included site, is reasonable. The breaking design is probably justified because the less-breaking path would be incomplete and would leave receivers reconciling a deprecated root site with the new repeating backbone indefinitely.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `BodyStructure.location` as a deprecated alias and added `includedStructure` for richer R6 structure details. That would keep many R4 instances using a single root location valid, but it would not satisfy a strict requirement that every instance use `includedStructure.structure`, and it would create long-term duplicate same-resource representations for the same anatomical site.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common single-site R4 instances, but duplicates site representation and still cannot preserve locationless R4 instances if R6 requires an included structure.

evidence.detail: R4 `location` is 0..1 CodeableConcept bound at example strength to body-site.
R6 adds required `includedStructure` 1..*.
R6 requires `includedStructure.structure` 1..1 CodeableConcept.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 fragment uses the R4-required `patient`; root `location` must become an R6 `includedStructure` entry.

findings.narrativeMd: `BodyStructure.location` was not simply renamed. R6 remodels BodyStructure around a required repeating `includedStructure` backbone, changing validators, generated model properties, FHIRPath paths, indexing code, and assumptions that there is only one root body site.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs when an R4 BodyStructure omits `location` or contains root `location` without the new `includedStructure.structure`. A valid R6 instance with one included structure can often be down-converted to R4 `location`, but multiple included structures are not lossless.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create `includedStructure[0].structure` from R4 `location` when present. If location is absent, derive it, reject the record for R6, or use an implementation-specific extension/profile policy. Test missing, single, and multiple anatomy cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The expressive model appears justified, but mandatory adoption and removal of the old path are the breaking parts. Deprecated root aliases and consistency checks would have been less disruptive but more ambiguous.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed for records without location and for systems deciding whether multiple R6 included structures are allowed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 represented the anatomical site at optional root `BodyStructure.location`; R6 replaces that with required repeating `includedStructure`, whose `structure` is 1..1. A raw R4 instance using `location` is not R6-shaped, and an R4 instance with only patient/description has no obvious required R6 structure to populate. For ordinary single-site instances the migration is usually mechanical, and the R6 goal of supporting multiple included/excluded structures with per-structure details is coherent.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.location` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with example body-site binding.
R6 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.includedStructure` is 1..* and `includedStructure.structure` is 1..1 CodeableConcept.
HL7 mCODE Tumor Profile v4.0.0 profiles R4 BodyStructure for tumor tracking and makes `BodyStructure.location` 1..1 must-support.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 1/trial-use softens the stability expectation. mCODE shows real oncology use of the path, so the break is not dismissed, but the low base maturity and coherent remodel keep it below Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old wire instances with root `location` and no R6 `includedStructure.structure` need transformation before R6 validation; generated paths and queries also change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could retain root `location` as a deprecated alias while adding `includedStructure`, but that creates duplicate site representations and precedence rules once multiple structures or excluded structures exist. That alternative is only partial and has material model-cleanliness cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing hard-break concern and partial-alternative assessment, but the FMM 1 context and duplicate-representation tradeoff make the break probably acceptable.

findings.title: Morphology moved from resource root to each included structure

oldState.summary: R4 had one optional top-level morphology, 0..1 CodeableConcept.

semanticText.definition: The kind of structure being represented by the body structure at `BodyStructure.location`.

oldState.narrativeMd: Morphology applied to the whole R4 BodyStructure.

newState.summary: R6 has optional morphology 0..1 on each includedStructure.

semanticText.definition: The kind of structure being represented by the body structure at `BodyStructure.location`.

newState.narrativeMd: Morphology is scoped to a particular included structure.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Name, type, cardinality, and binding match, but the element is nested in R6.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing root `morphology` is not an R6 instance. R6 can express different morphologies for different included or excluded structures, while R4 had only one root morphology.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Morphology can distinguish normal anatomy from lesions or abnormalities.

justification.inferredGoal: Scope morphology to the anatomy component it describes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep root `morphology` as a deprecated shortcut for single-included-structure cases while adding per-structure morphology.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Scoping morphology to the included structure is a reasonable goal once BodyStructure can represent multiple structures. The old root element cannot unambiguously describe which structure has the morphology in richer R6 instances, so the break is probably justified despite an incomplete compatibility path.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would preserve root `morphology` as deprecated and define that it applies only when there is exactly one included structure or when it is consistent with all per-structure values. That preserves common R4 cases but requires conflict rules and risks deprecated root morphology becoming a permanent parallel representation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Helps simple R4 instances, but becomes ambiguous for multiple structures and duplicates morphology facts across root and backbone paths.

evidence.detail: R4 defines root `morphology` 0..1 CodeableConcept.
R6 defines `includedStructure.morphology` 0..1 CodeableConcept and no root morphology.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes morphology from a resource-level attribute into an attribute of an included structure. This is a serialized-instance break and a semantic change because morphology is now tied to a specific anatomy component.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 root `morphology` is invalid in R6 until transformed. R6 instances with one included structure can be represented in R4, but multiple structures with different morphologies cannot be represented without loss or extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move R4 `morphology` into the `includedStructure` created from `location`. Down-converters should reject, extend, or manually review R6 instances with more than one distinct morphology.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The move is semantically clean, but a deprecated root alias could have preserved simple old instances at the cost of ambiguity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The bodystructure-code ValueSet compose changed as well; see the terminology finding.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 had optional root `BodyStructure.morphology`; R6 removes the root element and adds `includedStructure.morphology`. Existing instances, FHIRPath, generated models, and profiles that refer to the root path must be updated. For a single included structure the data move is mostly mechanical, while the R6 design usefully scopes morphology to the anatomical component it describes.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.morphology` is 0..1 CodeableConcept.
R6 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.includedStructure.morphology` is 0..1 CodeableConcept and no root `morphology` exists.
HL7 mCODE Tumor Profile v4.0.0 uses R4 `BodyStructure.morphology` as a must-support tumor element with an extensible tumor morphology binding.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 1/trial-use lowers the compatibility burden for base redesign. The mCODE evidence shows implementation relevance, so this remains a real migration issue rather than harmless churn.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old instances and generated APIs using root `morphology` need path migration to `includedStructure.morphology`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could keep root `morphology` as a deprecated single-structure shortcut, but it would be ambiguous or conflicting when an instance has multiple included structures. The alias would preserve simple R4 instances but at the cost of two ways to represent the same morphology fact.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree that the old path is broken and the alternative is only partial; I would emphasize the mCODE impact but still consider the redesign proportionate.

findings.title: Location qualifiers moved and split into per-structure qualifier, laterality, and landmark-orientation elements

oldState.summary: R4 had root `locationQualifier` 0..* CodeableConcept for laterality, relative location, directionality, number, and plane.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Comparison uses packaged compose concepts, not full SNOMED expansion.

semanticText.definition: Qualifier to refine the anatomical location.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 stored all location qualifiers in one root repeating list.

newState.summary: R6 has per-structure `qualifier` 0..*, separate `laterality` 0..1, and `bodyLandmarkOrientation` details.

semanticText.short: Code that represents the included structure qualifier
semanticText.definition: Code that represents the included structure qualifier.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates laterality and landmark-relative details from generic qualifiers.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old element maps partly to `qualifier`, partly to `laterality`, and partly to new landmark-orientation structures.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Root `locationQualifier` is not valid in R6. A mechanical rename is insufficient because laterality now has a separate 0..1 element and landmark details use a nested backbone.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Laterality and relative-location errors can point consumers to the wrong side or sub-location.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate laterality and landmark-relative anatomy details from generic location qualifiers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain root `locationQualifier` as a deprecated catch-all while adding per-structure `qualifier`, `laterality`, and landmark-orientation elements.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating laterality and landmark-relative details from a broad catch-all qualifier is a reasonable R6 goal. The less-breaking design is only partial because it preserves ambiguity and requires clinical/terminology reconciliation when the same fact can appear in both old and new locations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A compatibility-oriented base design could keep `BodyStructure.locationQualifier` and introduce the new structured fields as preferred destinations. This would preserve R4 instances but would not provide a clean, single representation for laterality and landmark details, and without authoritative ConceptMaps it could make receivers guess which field is authoritative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids old-path rejection but leaves competing qualifier/laterality representations, unclear precedence, and safety-sensitive mapping burden.

evidence.detail: R4 root `locationQualifier` is 0..* and includes laterality in its definition.
R6 defines per-structure `qualifier`.
R6 adds separate `laterality` bound to bodystructure-laterality.
Relative-location compose changed and R6 adds a separate laterality ValueSet.

examples.examplesMd: The code mapping is illustrative; production transforms need terminology review or a ConceptMap.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 decomposes the broad R4 `locationQualifier` field. Existing qualifiers must be moved under the correct included structure, and laterality-like qualifiers may need code translation into `includedStructure.laterality`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with root `locationQualifier` are invalid in R6 until transformed. R6 per-structure laterality or landmark orientation cannot be round-tripped to R4 without flattening or extensions, which loses context.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify each R4 qualifier. Map true laterality to `includedStructure.laterality`, retained relative-location qualifiers to `includedStructure.qualifier`, and landmark-specific data to `bodyLandmarkOrientation` only when source data supports that meaning.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split improves semantic precision, but preserving `locationQualifier` as a deprecated catch-all would have avoided direct instance breakage at the cost of continued ambiguity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Laterality migration needs clinical/terminology review because no official ConceptMap was available locally.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `locationQualifier` was a repeatable root catch-all for laterality, relative location, directionality, number, and plane. R6 removes that path and splits the content across per-structure `qualifier`, `laterality`, and landmark-orientation fields. The structural goal is reasonable, but migration is not just a rename: laterality and qualifier codes may need clinical/terminology classification, and mistakes in laterality are safety-significant.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.locationQualifier` is 0..* CodeableConcept and its definition explicitly includes laterality.
R6 StructureDefinition: `includedStructure.qualifier` is 0..*, `includedStructure.laterality` is 0..1, and landmark-orientation subelements are separate.
R4 relative-location ValueSet includes Unilateral left/right and Bilateral; R6 moves Bilateral plus Left/Right qualifier values into `bodystructure-laterality` and changes the relative-location list.
HL7 mCODE Tumor Profile v4.0.0 uses R4 `BodyStructure.locationQualifier` as a must-support element with a required body-location/laterality qualifier value set.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 1/trial-use would normally soften a structural break, but the path carries clinical laterality and has official oncology IG use. That safety and implementation evidence raises the need for a more compatibility-conscious transition.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the old root field is no longer valid, and correct migration may require classifying each qualifier as laterality, generic qualifier, or landmark orientation rather than copying a property name.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A transitional base design could retain deprecated root `locationQualifier` for one release or explicitly allow legacy qualifier concepts in the new split fields while recommending the structured destinations. This would preserve old instances and reduce laterality-mapping risk, with tradeoffs of duplicate representations and precedence rules. Given the safety relevance, that tradeoff deserves renewed standards review.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree that the split has a valid modeling goal and only a partial alternative, but I rate the current design more concerning than the existing report because of laterality safety and mCODE usage.

findings.title: Patient reference became optional, creating R6-to-R4 validation and business-rule risk

semanticText.definition: The person to which the body site belongs.

oldState.narrativeMd: Every valid R4 BodyStructure identified a Patient subject.

semanticText.definition: The person to which the body site belongs.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows a BodyStructure without a Patient reference.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Relaxing minimum cardinality does not invalidate R4 instances in R6, but a valid R6 BodyStructure without `patient` cannot validate as R4. R4-era code may also dereference patient without null handling.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Patientless anatomy data can be unsafe or unusable in patient-specific workflows unless context supplies the patient.

justification.inferredGoal: Permit body-structure definitions or anatomy records not tied to one patient.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible alternative is needed because lowering `patient` minimum cardinality preserves R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of allowing patientless BodyStructure instances may be reasonable, but the local inputs do not explain why the base resource needed to relax `patient`. Under the calibration rules, this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue because R4 instances with `patient` remain valid with respect to this element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping `patient` required would preserve the R4 guarantee, but that is not a less-breaking alternative for an R4-to-R6 validation break; there is no such break here. Local R6 profiles or R6-to-R4 transform policies can require a patient for specific workflows, but those are mitigations for down-conversion and runtime assumptions rather than base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 conversion and nullable-runtime risk, not old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 breakage.

evidence.detail: R4 `patient` is min 1, max 1, target Patient.
R6 `patient` is min 0, max 1, same Patient target.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 weakens `BodyStructure.patient` from required to optional. This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but it materially affects bidirectional systems and R4-oriented code because `patient` was previously guaranteed.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to `patient` in R6. A valid R6 BodyStructure without `patient` is not R4-representable unless a patient can be supplied from trusted context.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R6-to-R4 transforms must require a patient reference, derive it from trusted context, or reject conversion. R6 generated-code users should treat patient as nullable.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The relaxation could have been avoided by using profiles for patientless cases, preserving down-conversion at the cost of constraining the base model.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 relaxes `BodyStructure.patient` from required to optional. This does not make any R4 instance invalid in R6, because every R4-valid instance already has the patient reference. The practical concern is reverse conversion or R6 client code that assumed all BodyStructure instances are patient-specific, but patient-specific workflows can retain the R4 guarantee with profiles.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.patient` is 1..1 Reference(Patient).
R6 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.patient` is 0..1 Reference(Patient).
HL7 R4 BodyStructure scope says the resource supports tracking an anatomical location on a patient; mCODE Tumor Profile keeps `patient` 1..1 for its oncology workflow.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 1/trial-use softens concern about broadening the base resource. The mCODE evidence shows patient-specific profiles matter, but those profiles can still require `patient`.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: patientless R6 instances cannot be faithfully represented as R4 BodyStructure without inventing a patient; R4-to-R6 validation is not broken.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `patient` required would preserve the R4 semantic guarantee, but it would block the R6 goal of patientless or definitional anatomical structures. Requiring patient in profiles is the cleaner compatibility mechanism for patient-specific workflows.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing conclusion that this is not an R4-to-R6 hard break; I would down-rank the impact to no base-design problem despite reverse-conversion awareness.

findings.title: Description primitive type changed from string to markdown

semanticText.definition: A summary, characterization or explanation of the body structure.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 treated description as plain string content.

semanticText.definition: A summary, characterization or explanation of the body structure.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 explicitly permits markdown processing for the same description element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The wire shape remains a JSON string, so ordinary R4 string values should parse as R6 markdown. The main risk is generated-code, UI rendering, escaping, and sanitization behavior.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Rendering untrusted markdown without sanitization can create display or security issues.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that explanatory text may contain markdown formatting.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `description` typed as `string` and document that markdown formatting is allowed by convention.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The markdown goal is understandable, and the wire format remains a JSON string, but changing the primitive type still creates generated-code and rendering assumptions. Because the same practical goal could be met by clearer definition text while keeping the R4 type, this break was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design would retain `BodyStructure.description` as `string` and state in the definition/comment that implementations may include markdown syntax. This preserves essentially all R4-valid instances and old generated models while still telling implementers how to render the field, though it gives validators and code generators a weaker semantic signal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves instance and generated-type stability with low-to-moderate cost: tooling loses a first-class markdown signal and must rely on comments or profiles.

evidence.detail: R4 type is string.
R6 type is markdown.
Local primitive definitions show markdown derives from string and serializes through a string value.

findings.narrativeMd: `description` changes from `string` to `markdown`. This is mainly a generated-code and rendering change, not an expected instance-validation break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 strings and R6 markdown both serialize as JSON strings. R6 markdown can be stored in R4 as a string, but R4 applications may display markup literally.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update type annotations and UI rendering assumptions. Treat markdown as untrusted user-facing content unless the rendering pipeline already sanitizes it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been avoided by comments alone, but using markdown gives tooling stronger semantic information.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `BodyStructure.description` changes from `string` to `markdown`, but markdown is a string-derived primitive and the wire value is still a JSON string. Existing plain text remains valid markdown, and systems are not required to render markdown. Some generated SDKs may expose a different primitive type, but this optional descriptive field does not create a meaningful base instance-compatibility problem.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.description` type is `string`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `BodyStructure.description` type is `markdown`.
R6 `StructureDefinition-markdown` has baseDefinition `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/string` and defines markdown as a string that may contain GitHub Flavored Markdown.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 1/trial-use further softens a minor optional-field primitive refinement.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: some generated models may distinguish string from markdown, but old serialized values remain strings and should remain acceptable as markdown text.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could leave the type as `string` and mention markdown in prose. That would be slightly more stable for generated APIs, but it would also provide a weaker computable signal. Because the compatibility effect is small, the alternative does not warrant a Revisit judgment.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the existing report identified a real less-breaking alternative, but I do not think the optional string-derived markdown change has enough practical compatibility impact to be a problem.

findings.title: R6 adds included/excluded structure details that R4 cannot represent losslessly

oldState.summary: R4 had a flat model with one root location, root morphology, root locationQualifier, root image, and patient.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has no local elements for excluded structures, landmark orientation, distance from landmark, spatial imaging reference, or per-structure image.

newState.summary: R6 adds repeating includedStructure, excludedStructure, bodyLandmarkOrientation, spatialReference to ImagingSelection, per-structure images, laterality, and device/distance detail.

semanticText.definition: R6 can represent included and excluded anatomy regions, landmark-relative positioning, imaging coordinate references, and per-structure details.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 model is richer than the R4 BodyStructure content model.

facts.newValue: 0..* backbone with landmark, clock-face, distance, and surface orientation

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are new local BodyStructure elements, not inherited base fields.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional R6 additions do not by themselves invalidate old instances, but valid R6 instances using them cannot be serialized into R4 without extensions, flattening, or data loss.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of excluded-anatomy or spatial-reference detail can affect localization and imaging workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Support detailed anatomy localization and imaging/spatial use cases.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: The added R6 structure-detail elements are optional R6 content and do not create an R4-to-R6 old-valid/new-invalid break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: First-class included/excluded structure, landmark-orientation, spatial-reference, and per-structure image fields reasonably support richer localization use cases. Because these are optional R6 additions, the issue is chiefly down-conversion from R6 to R4 rather than avoidable R4-to-R6 base breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable under the calibration rules. Modeling these details only as extensions on an R4-shaped resource could help R6-to-R4 round-tripping, but that is an extension/backport workaround and would sacrifice the discoverability and interoperability of first-class R6 elements.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 loss remains, but extension/backport or flattening strategies are conversion mitigations, not less-breaking R6 base designs.

evidence.detail: R6 `excludedStructure` is 0..* and content-references `includedStructure`.
R6 adds landmark, clock-face, distance, device, and surface-orientation children.
R6 adds 0..* Reference(ImagingSelection).
R4 has no excludedStructure, landmark orientation, spatialReference, or per-structure image.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds substantial BodyStructure content beyond moved R4 fields. Systems that must consume R6 and emit R4 need explicit policies because flattening loses which details applied to which included or excluded anatomy.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Valid R6 instances using these new paths are rejected by strict R4 validators and have no R4 generated-class properties. Old R4 instances are not broken by these additions after migration.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, reject unsupported details, preserve them in extensions, or flatten only when unambiguous and clinically safe. Test excluded structures, spatialReference, per-structure images, and landmark distances.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The expressivity is likely justified. Extension-based alternatives would preserve compatibility but reduce first-class interoperability.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm exact R6 instance examples with an R6 validator when building production transforms.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The cited R6 elements, including `excludedStructure`, landmark orientation details, spatial reference, and per-structure image, are optional additions. They do not reject R4 instances. They can be lossy when converting rich R6 instances back to R4, but that is expected for genuinely new R6 expressivity rather than an avoidable R4-to-R6 base break.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `excludedStructure` is 0..* and content-references `includedStructure`.
R6 StructureDefinition: landmark description, clock-face position, distance from landmark, surface orientation, `spatialReference`, and per-structure `image` are optional.
R4 StructureDefinition has no corresponding excluded-structure, landmark-orientation, or spatial-reference elements.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 1/trial-use lowers stability concern, and optional additive R6 content is the kind of evolution expected for low-maturity material.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: new optional R6 localization details may not fit into R4 without extensions or narrative, but R4-to-R6 instances are not made invalid by the additions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4 preservation. Modeling all new detail only as extensions would improve round-tripping but would sacrifice first-class discoverability and interoperability; that is a conversion mitigation, not a better base model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report treated this mainly as R6-to-R4 loss with no applicable less-breaking base alternative, which matches my assessment.

findings.title: BodyStructure terminology bindings and ValueSet contents changed, mainly as semantic and pick-list risk

oldState.summary: R4 used example bindings for body-site, bodystructure-code, and bodystructure-relative-location. The R4 morphology ValueSet filter used SNOMED concept 49755003; relative-location included unilateral left/right/bilateral.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 terminology bindings were not required, but implementations may have used them for pick lists or profile constraints.

newState.summary: R6 retains example bindings on many fields but changes compose definitions, adds laterality and clock-face ValueSets, and introduces a preferred surfaceOrientation binding.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Full SNOMED expansions were not available.

newState.narrativeMd: Canonical URLs are partly stable, but compose filters and concept lists changed.

facts.newValue: 40 explicit SNOMED concepts plus SNOMED is-a 442083009
adds distal/dorsal/plantar and moves laterality to separate ValueSet

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The compared ValueSets are directly referenced by local BodyStructure elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Most affected bindings are example or preferred strength, so base-resource validation does not hard-fail because of code-set differences. Local profiles, terminology validation modes, UI pick lists, and analytics may still change behavior.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Changed anatomy, morphology, and laterality code sets can affect clinical selection and downstream logic.

justification.inferredGoal: Align ValueSets with the restructured anatomy model and more precise SNOMED subsets.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use transitional broader R6 example/preferred ValueSets that include legacy concepts where semantically safe; ConceptMaps alone are migration aids, not base alternatives.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning terminology with the restructured anatomy model is plausible, and example/preferred binding strengths limit base validation breakage. However, without official rationale, SNOMED expansions, or ConceptMaps, the necessity and safety of the specific ValueSet changes cannot be fully assessed.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would be transitional ValueSets that temporarily retain old unilateral qualifier concepts and compatible morphology/site concepts while adding the new R6 concepts. That is only a partial alternative: it does not solve structural mapping, can leave duplicate codes for the same clinical idea, and may reduce terminology precision. Publishing ConceptMaps would be helpful migration guidance but should not be counted as the backward-compatible base design itself.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Could ease pick-list and warning-mode compatibility, but may duplicate laterality semantics, broaden morphology/site choices, and create analytics or safety ambiguity without expansion evidence.

evidence.detail: R4 bodystructure-code filter is SNOMED concept is-a 49755003.
R6 bodystructure-code filter is SNOMED concept is-a 118956008.
R4 relative-location listed unilateral left/right/bilateral; R6 moves laterality to a separate ValueSet and changes relative-location concepts.
R6 surfaceOrientation has preferred binding to bodystructure-relative-location.

examples.examplesMd: No code fragment can prove expansion-level compatibility without terminology-server expansion.

findings.narrativeMd: Terminology changes are not base-resource hard breaks because the bindings are mostly example/preferred, but they are important for systems that use core ValueSets as pick lists, warnings, profile constraints, or analytics dimensions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base R4 codes outside R6 example ValueSets should still validate against base R6 binding strength. Stricter local profiles or enum-like generated lists can reject or mishandle codes unless mappings are updated.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory local binding-strength overrides and pick lists. Update terminology services for R6 ValueSets and build or obtain ConceptMaps for R4 unilateral qualifiers and morphology filter changes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Compatibility would be improved by official ConceptMaps and transitional ValueSets. Without them, implementers need human-reviewed mappings.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confidence is medium because SNOMED expansions and official cross-version maps were unavailable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The BodyStructure-related ValueSets changed, including the SNOMED filter behind `bodystructure-code` and the split of laterality concepts from relative-location. At the base StructureDefinition level, the relevant bindings on morphology, structure, qualifier, and laterality are example strength, and the landmark surface-orientation binding is preferred. These changes can affect UI pick lists, terminology caches, and profile authors, but they do not make base instances invalid.
keyEvidence: R4 `ValueSet-bodystructure-code` uses SNOMED filter concept is-a 49755003; R6 uses concept is-a 118956008.
R4 relative-location ValueSet includes Unilateral left/right and Bilateral; R6 relative-location removes the unilateral concepts and adds a separate laterality ValueSet.

R6 StructureDefinition bindings for `includedStructure.morphology`, `includedStructure.qualifier`, and `includedStructure.laterality` are example strength; `bodyLandmarkOrientation.surfaceOrientation` is preferred.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 1/trial-use softens concern. Because the base bindings are example/preferred rather than required/extensible, low maturity reinforces treating this as metadata/tooling churn rather than a base break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: terminology expansions, pick lists, and documentation may change, but base validators should not reject an old CodeableConcept solely because these example/preferred ValueSets changed.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could publish broader transitional example ValueSets or ConceptMaps to ease migration, but those would mainly be guidance and tooling aids. Since base conformance is not tightened, a less-breaking base design is not necessary.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the existing report treated the terminology change as uncertain with a partial alternative; I find the base compatibility risk low because the bindings are not required.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 counterpart is present at the same canonical URL and type, with kind `resource`, type `BodyStructure`, base `DomainResource`, and abstract `false`.
No local BodyStructure-specific invariants were found in either snapshot beyond inherited/base constraints.
`BodyStructure.active` remains an optional boolean modifier with the same modifier reason and meaning-when-missing; new local BodyStructure elements are not modifiers.
The existing `patient` target remains Patient. R6 adds `includedStructure.spatialReference` to ImagingSelection, covered as R6-only conversion risk.
No local fixed values, pattern values, default values, value limits, maxLength, or regex restrictions were identified.
No local slicing rules were identified for BodyStructure elements in the R4 or R6 StructureDefinitions.
Corresponding local data elements keep materially similar summary behavior. Inherited `modifierExtension` summary flag changes are base-artifact scope and excluded.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Resource status changed from draft to active without canonical identity change
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Canonical URL, id, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. Status maturity affects governance, not instance wire compatibility.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat the R6 artifact as the current active definition, but do not infer a rename or replacement resource.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root image remains but R6 text emphasizes the overall structure
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `BodyStructure.image` retains path, cardinality 0..*, type Attachment, and non-summary/non-modifier flags.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Images tied to a specific included or excluded structure may be better migrated to `includedStructure.image`; resource-level images can remain at `BodyStructure.image`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Identifier and active remain structurally stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `identifier` remains 0..* Identifier and summary. `active` remains 0..1 boolean, summary, and modifier with the same meaning-when-missing.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Existing identifier and active handling should continue after generated-code package updates.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited DomainResource/Resource changes were excluded and should be handled by base-artifact reports.
R6 BodyStructure now relies heavily on local BackboneElement children; inherited BackboneElement behavior may affect generated code but is out of scope here.
Safe migration needs authoritative mappings, especially for unilateral left/right qualifiers and morphology ValueSet changes.
R6 `includedStructure.spatialReference` references ImagingSelection and has no R4 BodyStructure counterpart.
